{{short description|Austrian experimental physicist (born 1973)}}
'''Rupert Ursin''' (born January 26, 1973) is an Austrian experimental physicist active in the field of [[quantum entanglement]] and communications. He founded several companies, e.g. Quantum Technology Laboratories GmbH.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.qtlabs.at/team/rupert-ursin/|title=Rupert Ursin|website=www.qtlabs.at|language=en|access-date=2023-12-05}}</ref> and Quantum Industries GmbH <ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.quantum-industries.eu/#team|title=Rupert Ursin|website=www.quantum-industries.eu|language=en|access-date=2023-12-05}}.</ref> and acts currently as CEO in both of theses companies.

== Education ==
Ursin completed his [[Master's degree|Masters diploma]] in 2001, then in December 2006 completed a PhD [[dissertation]] at [[University of Vienna]] on [[quantum teleportation]] over long distances under the guidance of [[Anton Zeilinger]]. He continued with postdoctoral studies in 2007, and since 2013 has served as a research group leader and Deputy Director at the IQOQI.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Ursin's research group is active in the field of [[quantum entanglement]] and communications.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Aspect|first=Alain|date=2015-12-16|title=Viewpoint: Closing the Door on Einstein and Bohr's Quantum Debate|url=https://physics.aps.org/articles/v8/123|journal=Physics|language=en-US|volume=8|doi=10.1103/Physics.8.123|doi-access=free}}</ref> In particular, the team demonstrated an example of loophole-free [[Bell's theorem|Bell inequality]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Giustina|first1=Marissa|last2=Versteegh|first2=Marijn A. M.|last3=Wengerowsky|first3=Sören|last4=Handsteiner|first4=Johannes|last5=Hochrainer|first5=Armin|last6=Phelan|first6=Kevin|last7=Steinlechner|first7=Fabian|last8=Kofler|first8=Johannes|last9=Larsson|first9=Jan-Åke|date=2015-12-16|title=Significant-Loophole-Free Test of Bell's Theorem with Entangled Photons|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=115|issue=25|article-number=250401|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.115.250401|pmid=26722905|arxiv=1511.03190|bibcode=2015PhRvL.115y0401G|s2cid=13789503}}</ref> and worked on [[quantum key distribution]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Steinlechner|first1=Fabian|last2=Ecker|first2=Sebastian|last3=Fink|first3=Matthias|last4=Liu|first4=Bo|last5=Bavaresco|first5=Jessica|last6=Huber|first6=Marcus|last7=Scheidl|first7=Thomas|last8=Ursin|first8=Rupert|date=2017-07-24|title=Distribution of high-dimensional entanglement via an intra-city free-space link|journal=Nature Communications|language=En|volume=8|article-number=15971|doi=10.1038/ncomms15971|doi-access=free|pmid=28737168|pmc=5527279|arxiv=1612.00751|bibcode=2017NatCo...815971S}}</ref>  

In 2004, Ursin and colleagues from the [[Institute for Experimental Physics]] at the University of Vienna succeeded in the world's-first demonstration of [[quantum teleportation]] of a [[photon]] outside of the laboratory, sending it a distance of 600 meters across the [[Danube|River Danube.]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/quantum-teleportation-acr/|title=Quantum Teleportation across the Danube Demonstrated|last=Graham|first=Sarah|work=Scientific American|access-date=2018-02-16|language=en}}</ref>

In 2007, Ursin's group succeeded in distributing [[Quantum entanglement|entangled photons]] between the [[Canary Islands]] [[La Palma]] and [[Tenerife]] over a world-record distance of 144 km.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ursin|first1=R.|last2=Tiefenbacher|first2=F.|last3=Schmitt-Manderbach|first3=T.|last4=Weier|first4=H.|last5=Scheidl|first5=T.|last6=Lindenthal|first6=M.|last7=Blauensteiner|first7=B.|last8=Jennewein|first8=T.|last9=Perdigues|first9=J.|date=2007|title=Entanglement-based quantum communication over 144 km|journal=Nature Physics|language=En|volume=3|issue=7|pages=481–486|doi=10.1038/nphys629|issn=1745-2481|bibcode=2007NatPh...3..481U|arxiv=quant-ph/0607182}}</ref>  

In 2016, Ursin's group successfully tested entanglement in [[accelerated reference frame]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fink|first1=Matthias|last2=Rodriguez-Aramendia|first2=Ana|last3=Handsteiner|first3=Johannes|last4=Ziarkash|first4=Abdul|last5=Steinlechner|first5=Fabian|last6=Scheidl|first6=Thomas|last7=Fuentes|first7=Ivette|author-link7=Ivette Fuentes |last8=Pienaar|first8=Jacques|last9=Ralph|first9=Timothy C.|date=2017-05-10|title=Experimental test of photonic entanglement in accelerated reference frames|journal=Nature Communications|language=En|volume=8|article-number=15304|doi=10.1038/ncomms15304|doi-access=free|pmid=28489082|pmc=5436216|bibcode=2017NatCo...815304F|arxiv=1608.02473}}</ref> and in a [[Zero-G flight]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1= Bittermann|first1= Julius Arthur|last2= Bulla |first2= Lukas |last3= Ecker |first3=Sebastian|last4= Neumann |first4= Sebastian Philipp|last5= Fink |first5= Matthias |last6= Bohmann |first6= Martin |last7= Friis |first7= Nicolai|last8= Huber |first8= Marcus|last9= Ursin |first9= Rupert |date=2024-02-15|title= Photonic entanglement during a zero-g flight |journal=Quantum|language=En|volume=8|page=1256|doi=10.22331/q-2024-02-15-1256|bibcode=2024Quant...8.1256B |arxiv=2303.13183}}</ref>
